facts.text: I compared a list of desired skills, knowledge, and qualifications for an Instructional Designer with a job description for an Instructional Designer position found on LinkedIn Jobs.
I used a method to indicate whether each list item was present in the LinkedIn job description.
I was given a list of 56 desired skills, knowledge, and qualifications for an Instructional Designer.
The job description was for an Instructional Designer position at a prestigious Ivy League university in Boston.
The role in the job description was hybrid and required local candidates.
The job description stated the role was a 6 month initial contract with the opportunity to extend or convert.
The job description said the Instructional Designer would work closely with faculty or business subject matter experts.
The job description said the Instructional Designer would design, create, and deliver online, blended, and instructor-led classroom training courses and documentation.
The job description said the work would use principles and practices of instructional design and adult learning theory.
The job description said responsibilities included developing content for learning or knowledge management systems.
The job description said responsibilities included conducting learning and business needs analysis.
The job description said responsibilities included drafting expected learning outcomes aligned with course goals and determining scope and sequence of content.
The job description said responsibilities included identifying impacted or target audiences and relevant pre-requisites for learner success.
The job description said responsibilities included designing and implementing course evaluation plans.
The job description said responsibilities included devising modes of assessment to measure course effectiveness.
The job description said responsibilities included writing effective copy, instructional materials, and audio/video scripts.
The job description said responsibilities included producing learning materials in print, graphics, audio, video, and multimedia formats.
The job description said the role would use e-learning authoring tools to upload instructional content to websites, e-learning platforms, or learning management systems.
The job description said the role may develop and deliver train-the-trainer programs and deliver in-person instruction of complex information.
The job description said the role would provide training on instructional technologies and tools.
The job description listed required skills and experience including a Master’s degree and formal training or certification in Instructional Design being preferable.
The job description listed required skills and experience including 3-5 years of professional experience in Instructional Design or Development.
The job description said the role required demonstrated experience with common web and multimedia authoring tools such as Adobe Captivate, Articulate Storyline, and Camtasia.
The job description said the role required knowledge of HTML.
The job description said the role required strong communication skills.
